content: Refresh tokens are invalidated server-side after each successful refresh, so the client must replace the stored refresh token every time.
The auth middleware should reject requests when the JWT is missing either sub or org_id because downstream authorization assumes both claims exist.
Login rate limiting is keyed by lowercased email plus IP, so aliases that normalize to the same email hit the same throttle bucket.
Confirmed again that refresh token rotation is enforced in the refresh handler and tests fail if the old token is reused.
I first thought refresh tokens were long-lived and reusable, but the code path actually revokes them after refresh. The old assumption is wrong.
Auth-related memory should tag both auth and the concrete mechanism like jwt, oauth, or refresh-token so future search is narrower.
Need to verify whether password reset tokens and login session tokens share the same revocation store.
The auth controller file is 312 lines long.
